Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 6, Verse 1

“The Blessed Lord said: One who performs the work that must be done without depending on its fruit is a renunciate and a yogin — not one who lights no fire and performs no rites.”

Krishna opens by stripping renunciation of its outward markers. The absence of ritual fires proves nothing; what counts is whether the work was done leaning on its results.
